prose.title: Stable radix sort from the ones place to the most significant digit

context: The input array nums contains ten eight-digit decimal integers, such as student IDs (the table gives their full values). Digit positions k start at 1. Digit 1, on the far right, is the least significant (ones), digit 2 is the tens digit, and so on up to digit 8, the most significant, on the far left (ten millions).
description: The four data columns show the input, the order after sorting by ones, the order after sorting by tens, and the final result. Read each column independently from top to bottom for array indices 0 through 9. A row shows the same current position in each state, not the path of one integer across passes. The five passes for digits 3 through 7 all run, although their intermediate states are omitted.

Each pass uses stable counting sort on the current digit. Two numbers with the same digit keep their relative order from the previous pass. For example, 35663510 and 88906420 both end in 0 and keep their original order after pass 1. The tens digits of 81883077 and 30524779 are both 7, so pass 2 retains their order from pass 1: 81883077, ending in 7, precedes 30524779, ending in 9.

More significant digits have higher priority when comparing numbers, so each later pass takes precedence over earlier ones. Where the higher digits are equal, stability preserves the order established by lower digits. Each pass moves entire eight-digit integers, never just the individual digits in one place.

frames.explanation: Starting with the least significant digit and preserving stability on every pass together ensure that the full values end up in order.

summary: Ten eight-digit integers are stably sorted one digit at a time, from digit 1 (ones) through digit 8 (ten millions), ending in ascending order by full numeric value.
